endorsements.quote: Given the evolving nature of AI technologies, simulation programmes will benefit from introducing AI-driven debriefing through small-scale pilot initiatives.

For simulation practitioners, this includes familiarity with the capabilities and limitations of generative AI systems, an understanding of how AI-generated outputs are produced, and the ability to critically appraise those outputs within educational contexts [ 16 , 23 ].
A foundational requirement for responsible implementation of AI is developing AI literacy among simulation practitioners [ 16 ].

Maintaining a ‘human-in-the-loop’ approach ensures that facilitators retain interpretative authority over AI-generated outputs and can critically evaluate AI-generated insights and integrate them appropriately within the broader educational context.

unlisted_practices: Align AI debriefing modes with clearly defined learning or organisational objectives before adoption.
Put policies for learner data collection, storage, access, and deletion in place before using AI debriefing tools.
Obtain informed consent from learners explaining how their data will be used and what safeguards protect their privacy.
Monitor AI debriefing tools for algorithmic bias.
Establish clear escalation pathways to human facilitators when AI systems generate uncertain or potentially misleading responses.
Implement cybersecurity safeguards against unauthorised access, data breaches, and misuse of sensitive learner data.
Treat AI implementation as an iterative process with continuous adjustment of prompts, workflows, governance structures, and faculty practices.
Constrain LLM outputs with explicit educational frameworks and structured prompts to improve interpretability and reduce output variability.
